title: Group by Even and Odd
prompt: A number sorter needs to split values into even and odd lanes. Write a function that returns an object { even, odd } where each key holds the matching numbers in their original order.

explanation.beginner:
Example: groupByParity([1,2,3,4]) produces {"even":[2,4],"odd":[1,3]}. Use a key-specific bucket or count so each occurrence changes only its own group.

Compare “handles all even”: input [[2,4,6]] produces {"even":[2,4,6],"odd":[]}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Use a key-specific bucket or count so each occurrence changes only its own group.

Tempting mistake: Reinitializing an existing group erases earlier contributions. Distinct-key counts differ from total occurrences.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles all even”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
